(RS_CRYPTO_02202)
7.4.1.10 Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM)
Briefly, a key encapsulation mechanism (
KEM
) works just like a public-key encryption
scheme, except that the encryption algorithm takes no input other than another key.
Therefore, the
KEM
uses randomly generated
Key Material
, the key encryption key
(
KEK
), to encapsulate an input, in this situation a key. The input is encapsulated with
an encryption with a target public key, as given in [27], [28], and [29]. The
KEK
can be
derived from the encapsulated
Key Material
or from randomly generated data by
application of a
KDF
.
